Containers, grouping and missing values

Source: vignettes/containers-and-missing-values.Rmd
containers-and-missing-values.Rmd

Most workflows can begin with Getting started, followed by category tables or measurement summaries. This companion explains what to expect when a result is a list, a group is missing, or a display shows only some rows.

Start with a tibble

This small illustration adapts the course survey, including a deliberately missing centre to show how grouping works.

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidystata)

survey <- tibble(
  centre = c("Riverside", "Riverside", "Hilltop", NA),
  satisfied = c("Yes", NA, "No", "Yes"),
  score = c(2, NA, 6, 8)
)

survey |> tab(satisfied)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   satisfied     n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr>     <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 No            1      25    25  33.3      33.3
#> 2 Yes           2      50    75  66.7     100  
#> 3 NA            1      25   100  NA        NA

With tibble inputs, the tab, summ, codebook and variables families return tibbles, including tables inside lists. Base data frames and data.table inputs retain their respective table class where supported. Other subclasses are not reconstructed on newly shaped tables; data.table summaries do not retain keys or indexes.

corr(), pwcorr(), spearman(), misstable() and duplicates_report() always return tibbles. Functions designed to return vectors, such as ds() and row_mean(), still return vectors.

Choose tables or lists deliberately

Separate one-way tabulations return a named list by default. Extract a table by its name:

tables <- survey |> tab1(centre, satisfied)

tables[["satisfied"]]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   value     n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr> <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 No        1      25    25  33.3      33.3
#> 2 Yes       2      50    75  66.7     100  
#> 3 NA        1      25   100  NA        NA

To work with one tibble instead, combine the variable tables:

survey |> tab1(centre, satisfied, .type = "tibble")
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   variable  value         n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr>     <chr>     <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 centre    Hilltop       1      25    25  33.3      33.3
#> 2 centre    Riverside     2      50    75  66.7     100  
#> 3 centre    NA            1      25   100  NA        NA  
#> 4 satisfied No            1      25    25  33.3      33.3
#> 5 satisfied Yes           2      50    75  66.7     100  
#> 6 satisfied NA            1      25   100  NA        NA

Output options vary by function:

Option Where it is useful
"vector" The default vector of names from ds().
"list" Separate variable tables in tab1()/fre1(), or type families in summaries. A single summary family returns one table.
"table" One table in the input’s table class for ds(), summ() and tabstat().
"auto" Preserve the input’s table class in fre(), tab2() and fre2().
"tibble" Explicit tibble output where supported; combines one-way variable tables or summary families.
"flextable" Formatted output from supported tabulation functions, requiring the optional flextable package.

tab() has no .type argument. Multiple-pair or explicitly grouped tab2()/fre2() calls still return lists: .type controls each table inside. Correlations use .wide for layout; both layouts are tibbles.

Separate grouping keys from measurements

A missing centre is still a group, and does not make its observed response invalid:

survey |> tab(satisfied, .by = centre)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   centre    satisfied     n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr>     <chr>     <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 Hilltop   No            1     100   100   100       100
#> 2 Riverside Yes           1      50    50   100       100
#> 3 Riverside NA            1      50   100    NA        NA
#> 4 NA        Yes           1     100   100   100       100

The one-way/joint tabulation and summary families inherit group_by() groups unless .by replaces them. Their results are ungrouped. Cross-tabulations require an explicit .by to split by group.

In summaries, .missing = FALSE drops missing grouping keys. Numeric calculations always omit missing measured values. Tabulation percentages use a 0-100 scale, while summary valid_pct uses 0-1. The dedicated tab and summ articles demonstrate the denominators.

Handle empty and all-missing measurements

An empty input and an all-missing measurement have no observed values. They retain n = 0 and undefined statistics, including sum = NA:

survey |>
  slice_head(n = 0) |>
  summ(score, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   type      n   sum  mean
#>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl       0    NA    NA

Entirely missing summary columns emit a warning. A row sum follows a different convention: adding no observed items gives zero. A row mean stays missing.

tibble(item1 = c(NA_real_, 4), item2 = c(NA_real_, 6)) |>
  mutate(
    total = row_sum(pick(starts_with("item"))),
    average = row_mean(pick(starts_with("item")))
  )
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   item1 item2 total average
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1    NA    NA     0      NA
#> 2     4     6    10       5

Empty selections produce empty tabulation results; row helpers need at least one column. Matrix columns are unsupported by tabulation and column summaries.

Understand labels and special missing values

Variable labels describe columns; value labels describe particular codes. An SPSS-style export might distinguish a refusal from an unanswered question:

imported <- tibble(
  answer = haven::labelled_spss(
    c(1, 2, 99, NA),
    labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2, Refused = 99),
    na_values = 99,
    label = "Course satisfaction"
  )
)

imported |> fre(answer)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 6
#>   answer            n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr>         <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 Yes               1      25    25    50        50
#> 2 No                1      25    50    50       100
#> 3 Valid Total       2      50    NA   100        NA
#> 4 Refused           1      25    75    NA        NA
#> 5 NA                1      25   100    NA        NA
#> 6 Missing Total     2      50    NA    NA        NA
#> 7 Total             4     100    NA    NA        NA

Tabulations recognise ordinary, tagged and SPSS user-missing values as missing. Numeric summaries exclude them from calculations. decode() reads value labels, but does not itself turn every labelled refusal into ordinary NA. For calculations outside haven-aware functions, explicitly normalise special missing values with haven::zap_missing().

misstable() also accepts matrix and nested data-frame columns. Ordinary list columns count scalar NA elements as missing and NULL as observed. Structured columns use vctrs row-missingness rules; list-backed matrices have different cell conventions, detailed in the missingness reference.

Keep calendar units visible

When numeric and calendar measurements occur together, default summaries separate the type families. Here the date table’s SD retains duration units:

visits <- tibble(
  score = c(4, 8),
  day = readr::parse_date(c("2026-09-01", "2026-09-03"))
)
separate <- visits |> summ(.stat = c("n", "mean", "sd"))
#> A list is returned as statistics are heterogeneous.

separate[["date"]]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   name  type      n mean       sd           
#>   <chr> <chr> <int> <chr>      <drtn>       
#> 1 day   date      2 2026-09-02 1.414214 days

The numeric table keeps numeric statistics. In combined .type = "table" or "tibble" output, shared location columns become character. Spread columns become plain numbers: days for dates and seconds for date-times, with units shown in type.

Preview a table without removing rows

A longer course register is easier to inspect at its beginning and end:

register <- tibble(id = 1:12, points = (1:12)^2)
view <- register |> preview_headtail(n = 4)

view
#> # A tibble: 12 × 2
#>       id points
#>    <int>  <dbl>
#>  1     1      1
#>  2     2      4
#>  ⋮     ⋮      ⋮
#> 11    11    121
#> 12    12    144
#> # ... 8 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows.

The display budget is four data rows, with an omission marker between the beginning and end. All twelve rows remain available for calculations:

view |> summarise(participants = n(), total_points = sum(points))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   participants total_points
#>          <int>        <dbl>
#> 1           12          650

For a view across the whole ordered register, use interval previews:

register |> preview_interval(n = 4)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 2
#>       id points
#>    <int>  <dbl>
#>  1     1      1
#>  5     5     25
#>  8     8     64
#> 12    12    144
#> # ... 8 rows omitted between displayed positions; use print(x, n = Inf) to show
#> # all rows.

Sort first when position should represent a meaningful order. unpreview() removes the persistent display setting. Supported dplyr/tidyr operations carry preview settings forward while following their own grouping and container rules.

print_headtail() and print_interval() print once and invisibly return the complete input. Wrapping and unwrapping data.table inputs copies them; later native data.table mutations follow ordinary reference semantics. If removing source columns with as_dummy(.remove = TRUE) would leave a data.table with rows but no columns, retain an identifier or another source column.
